newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka closes firm on low dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka closes firm on low dollar demand.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed firm against the dollar on Tuesday as the greenback slid due to a lack of commercial demand, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.40, near the Central Bank's buying level, after opening at about the same level and dropping to the 58.42 during the day, they said.
"It was a very dull day. The market traded at the bottom," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
The Central Bank, going by the international weakening of the dollar, pushed the greenback down by 1.5 local cents and fixed buying and selling at 58.3976 and 59.5774.
"The Central Bank too has not been positive towards the dollar during the past several days. So there is no point in being in dollars these days," a Hatton National Bank dealer said.

Other dealers said the market has been at the bottom for the past three weeks primarily due to the lack of import covering. A slowdown in consumption has cut down on imports, which in turn has reduced demand for the dollar, they said.
Overnight call money closed at its opening level of 12 percent, dealers said.
